review.tagline: Small personal assistant that runs each agent in its own Linux container
review.summary: NanoClaw is a self-hosted assistant built on the Claude Agent SDK. A single Node host routes messages from channels such as Slack, Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp to per-agent containers, exchanging them through two SQLite files per session. Channels and alternative providers are installed per fork with /add-<name> skills, and customization is done by changing code with Claude Code rather than editing config files.
review.audience: Self-hosters wanting a container-isolated chat assistant with a small codebase
strengths: Agents run in Docker containers and only see explicitly mounted directories
Credentials are injected by a gateway, so agents never hold raw API keys
Small codebase: one host process, no microservices, two SQLite files per session
Per-agent-group memory, CLAUDE.md and scheduled tasks; many channels via skills
weaknesses: Default setup depends on Claude Code and an Anthropic credential
No config files or dashboard; customization and debugging go through Claude Code
Channels and non-Claude providers are not in trunk; each needs a skill install
Prebuilt hardened image and managed Slack app require a free account
needs: Needs Docker, Node.js 22+, pnpm 10+, Claude Code, Anthropic API credential, OneCLI Agent Vault (credential gateway)
Models: Claude (default), OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, Google, DeepSeek via OpenCode, Ollama local models
